title: Graphing a Shifted Three-Halves Power Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of y = (x + 2)^(3/2) + 1 by identifying its parent function, shifts, endpoint, domain, range, and y-intercept.
finalAnswer: \text{Parent } y = x^{3/2} \text{ shifted left } 2 \text{ and up } 1;\quad \text{Endpoint: } (-2, 1),\quad \text{Domain: } [-2, \infty),\quad \text{Range: } [1, \infty),\quad \text{y-intercept: } (0, 2\sqrt{2} + 1)

steps.title: Identify the Parent Function and Translations
steps.explanation: The parent function is y = x^(3/2) on [0, infinity). Replacing x with x + 2 shifts the graph 2 units to the left, and adding 1 shifts it 1 unit upward.
steps.why: The translation vector (-2, 1) maps the origin endpoint (0, 0) of y = x^(3/2) to (-2, 1).

steps.title: Determine the Domain and Range
steps.explanation: The square root in (x + 2)^(3/2) requires x + 2 >= 0, so x >= -2. Since (x + 2)^(3/2) covers [0, infinity), adding 1 yields the range [1, infinity).
steps.why: Even-indexed roots require a non-negative base, and adding 1 shifts the minimum output from 0 to 1.

steps.title: Locate Key Points and the y-Intercept
steps.explanation: The curve starts at (-2, 1) with a horizontal tangent and curves upward increasingly steeply through (-1, 2), (0, 2*sqrt(2) + 1), and (2, 9).
steps.why: Evaluating at x = -2, -1, 0, 2 provides exact coordinates along the curve.
